extracted.intended_audience: government contractors, contracting officers, and procurement/accounting personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards (ASPR/Federal procurement regs) for determining when various contractor costs are allowable, unallowable, or subject to limitation or special treatment under Government contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments for abnormal forfeitures
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments for possible future abnormal forfeitures shall be effected according to the following rules: (i) Abnormal forfeitures that are foreseeable and which can be currently evaluated with reasonable accuracy, by actuarial or other sound computation, shall be reflected by an adjustment of current costs otherwise allowable; and (ii) Abnormal forfeitures, not within subdivision (i) of this subparagraph, may be made the subject of agreement between the Government and the contractor either as to an equitable adjustment or a method of determining such adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreseeable, quantifiable abnormal forfeitures -> adjust current allowable costs. Other abnormal forfeitures -> negotiate Government–contractor agreement (equitable adjustment or method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of deferred compensation (services now vs future)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether deferred compensation is for services rendered during the contract period or is for future services, consideration shall be given to conditions imposed upon eventual payment, such as requirements of consultation continued after retirement, and covenants not to compete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at contractual conditions tied to payment (e.g., post-retirement consultation or non-compete covenants) to decide whether compensation is allocable to current contract performance or is for future services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe benefits are allowances and services provided by the contractor to his employees as compensation in addition to regular wages and salaries. Costs of fringe benefits, such as pay for vacations, holidays, sick leave, military leave, employee insurance, and supplemental unemployment benefit plans are allowable to the extent required by law, employer-employee agreement, or an established policy of the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow fringe benefit costs only to the extent they are required by law, collective bargaining/employer-employee agreement, or an established contractor policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions and donations unallowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions and donations are unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No contract cost allowability for charitable contributions or donations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and repair costs—normal vs extraordinary
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs necessary for the upkeep of property which neither add to the permanent value nor appreciably prolong its intended life are treated as maintenance/repair: (1) Normal maintenance and repair costs are allowable; (2) Extraordinary maintenance and repair costs are allowable, provided such are allocated to the periods to which applicable for purposes of determining contract costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal upkeep = allowable; extraordinary maintenance allowable only if allocated to proper accounting periods (and subject to §15.107).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant and equipment expenditures must be capitalized
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenditures for plant and equipment, including rehabilitation thereof, which, according to generally accepted accounting principles as applied under the contractor’s established policy, should be capitalized and subjected to depreciation, are allowable only on a depreciation basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If GAAP/contractor policy requires capitalization, costs are allowable only via depreciation (not immediate expensing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocation costs—general allowability conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Relocation costs of certain types are allowable, provided (1) the move is for the benefit of the employer; (2) reimbursement is in accordance with an established policy or practice consistently followed by the employer and designed to motivate employees to relocate promptly and economically; (3) the costs are not otherwise unallowable under §15.205-33 or any other section; and (4) amounts reimbursed shall not exceed the employee’s actual (or reasonably estimated) expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relocation must benefit employer, be under consistent established policy, not otherwise unallowable, and reimbursed amounts limited to actual/reasonable estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocation costs—additional limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs otherwise allowable under relocation are subject to additional provisions: (1) the transition period for incurrence of certain relocation costs shall be kept to minimum necessary but in no event exceed a cumulative total of 30 days including advance trip time; and (2) allowance for cost of the type covered in paragraph (a)(3) shall not exceed 8 percent of the sales price of the property sold. Costs of the type covered in paragraph (a)(3) and (4) are allowable only in connection with relocation of existing employees and are not allowable for newly recruited employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes concrete numeric limits (30 days max transition; 8% maximum for certain costs) and restricts some payments to existing employees only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional and consultant service costs—general allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of professional and consultant services rendered by persons who are members of a particular profession or possess a special skill and who are not officers or employees of the contractor are allowable when reasonable in relation to the services rendered and when not contingent upon recovery of the costs from the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow professional/consultant costs if reasonable, not contingent on Government recovery, and subject to listed relevant factors and exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional services—relevant factors for allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining allowability, no single factor is necessarily determinative. Relevant factors include: (1) nature and scope of the service in relation to required service; (2) necessity considering contractor capability; (3) past pattern of such costs; (4) impact of Government contracts on the contractor’s business; (5) proportion of Government work to contractor’s total business; (6) whether service can be performed more economically by employment rather than contracting; (7) qualifications of the individual or concern and customary fees; (8) adequacy of contractual agreement for the service (description, estimate of time, rate, termination provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these factors holistically to judge reasonableness and necessity of professional/consultant costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retainer fees for consultants must be supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Retainer fees to be allowable must be supported by evidence of bona fide services available or rendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retainer payments require documentation showing real services either provided or available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain legal/accounting/consulting costs unallowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of legal, accounting, and consulting services, and related costs, incurred in connection with organization and reorganization, defense of antitrust suits, and the prosecution of claims against the Government, are unallowable. Costs incurred in connection with patent infringement litigation are unallowable unless otherwise provided for in the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify subject matter of legal/accounting services—if organizational, antitrust defense, or claim prosecution against Government (or patent infringement absent contract provision) -> unallowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rental costs—reasonableness standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Rental costs of land, building, equipment and other personal property are allowable if the rates are reasonable in light of factors such as rental costs of comparable facilities and market conditions in the area, the type, life expectancy, condition, and value of the facilities leased, options available, and other provisions of the rental agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare to market and ownership-equivalent costs; consider type, condition, options, and other lease provisions when judging reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intercompany rent under common control limited to normal ownership costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges in the nature of rent between plants, divisions, or organizations under common control are allowable to the extent such charges do not exceed the normal costs of ownership, such as depreciation, taxes, insurance, and maintenance, provided no part of such costs duplicates any other allowed costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intercompany rental cannot exceed normal ownership costs and must avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sale-and-leaseback rentals limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Rental costs specified in sale and leaseback agreements are allowable only to the extent that such rentals do not exceed the amount which the contractor would have received had he retained legal title to the facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sale-and-leaseback rentals capped at what contractor would have received if retained title; analysis required to compare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selling costs—allowability and allocability
rubrics_metrics.description: Selling costs (sales promotions, negotiation, liaison, etc.) are allowable to the extent they are reasonable and allocable to Government business. Allocability will be determined in light of reasonable benefit to the Government arising from activities such as technical, consulting, demonstration, and other services for application or adaptation of the contractor’s products to Government use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selling costs must be reasonable and demonstrably allocable to Government benefit—focus on technical/demo/adaptation activities that benefit Government use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salesmen/agents compensation contingent on award limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Salesmen's or agents' compensation, fees, commissions, percentages, or brokerage fees which are contingent upon the award of contracts are allowable only when paid to bona fide employees or bona fide established commercial or selling agencies maintained by the contractor for the purpose of securing business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contingent commission payments permitted only to bona fide employees or bona fide external selling agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severance pay—general allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Severance pay is allowable only to the extent that, in each case, it is required by (1) law, (2) employer-employee agreement, (3) established policy that constitutes, in effect, an implied agreement on the contractor’s part, or (4) circumstance of the particular employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Severance payments must be mandated by law/contract/policy or tied to particular employment circumstances to be allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severance pay—normal vs abnormal treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual normal turnover severance payments shall be allocated to all work performed in the contractor’s plant; accruals for normal severances acceptable if reasonable in light of past payments and allocated to all work. Abnormal or mass severance pay accruals are not allowable; however, Government may consider allowability case-by-case and participate to extent of fair share when such an event occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish normal (allocable or reasonably accrued) from abnormal/mass severance (no accruals; case-by-case Government participation possible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes—general allowability and explicit exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxes levied by Federal, State, or local governments are generally allowable if paid or accrued in accordance with GAAP, except for: (1) Federal income and excess profits taxes; (2) taxes in connection with financing/refinancing/refunding operations; (3) taxes from which exemptions are available to the contractor directly or via Government exemption (unless contracting officer finds exemption administratively burdensome); (4) special assessments on land representing capital improvements; (5) taxes on property used solely in connection with non-Government work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most taxes allowable under GAAP except listed categories; allocate taxes on property/work-in-process to the work benefited unless amounts insignificant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes contested or claimed illegal—procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxes otherwise allowable but upon which a claim of illegality or erroneous assessment exists are allowable provided the contractor, prior to payment, (1) promptly requests instructions from the contracting officer concerning such taxes; and (2) takes all action directed by the contracting officer (including cooperation to determine legality or secure a refund). Reasonable costs of such action directed by the contracting officer are allowable. Interest and penalties incurred due to nonpayment at contracting officer direction or due to contracting officer's failure to assure timely direction are also allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prescribed steps before paying contested taxes to preserve allowability; document requests and actions taken per contracting officer direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax refunds and interest credited to Government
rubrics_metrics.description: Any refund of taxes, interest, or penalties, and any payment to the contractor of interest thereon, attributable to taxes, interest, or penalties which were allowed as contract costs, shall be credited or paid to the Government as directed. Interest actually paid or credited to a contractor incident to a refund shall be paid or credited to the Government only to the extent that such interest accrued over the period during which the contractor had been reimbursed by the Government for the taxes, interest or penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refunds must be returned/credited to Government; interest treatment limited to the reimbursed reimbursement period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel costs—definition and allowable treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel costs include costs of transportation, lodging, subsistence, and incidental expenses incurred by contractor personnel in a travel status while on official company business. Travel costs may be based on actual costs, or on a per diem or mileage basis, or combination, provided the method does not result in an unreasonable charge. Travel in normal administration is allowable as indirect costs; travel directly attributable to specific contract performance is allowable as direct cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reasonable cost basis (actual/per diem/mileage); classify as indirect or direct depending on whether travel is general administration or contract-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air travel—first-class difference unallowable except specific circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The difference in cost between first-class air accommodations and less than first-class air accommodations is unallowable except when less than first-class accommodations are not reasonably available to meet necessary mission requirements, such as when less than first-class would: (1) require circuitous routing; (2) require travel during unreasonable hours; (3) greatly increase the duration of the flight; (4) result in additional costs which would offset the transportation savings; (5) offer accommodations not reasonably adequate for the physical or medical needs of the traveler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow first-class only when less-than-first-class would create substantial mission-related disadvantages among enumerated conditions; otherwise difference unallowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor-owned/leased/chartered aircraft—allowability and factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of contractor owned, leased, and chartered aircraft (lease, charter, operation, maintenance, depreciation, insurance, and related costs) are allowable, if reasonable, to the extent the contractor can demonstrate that use of such aircraft is necessary for the conduct of his business and that any increase in cost compared with alternative means is commensurate with the advantages gained. Factors to consider include: availability of scheduled commercial airlines at reasonable times; likelihood of critical/emergency situations; scheduling flexibility/time savings; security/privacy needs; contract requirement for flight testing. When need demonstrated, consider number/type/size of aircraft, method of acquisition, appropriateness of aircraft selected, and make optimum use where cost advantage to Government results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require demonstration of necessity and cost-justification; evaluate a multi-factor test including alternatives availability and mission needs; consider acquisition method and efficient utilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic planning costs—allowable as indirect costs with exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic planning costs (generalized long-range management planning concerned with future overall development of the contractor’s business) are allowable as indirect costs to be properly allocated. Research and development and engineering costs assigned to lead to new products for sale to the general public are not allowable under this provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow general economic planning as allocable indirect cost; exclude R&D/engineering intended to create new commercial products under this category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic data processing equipment (ADPE) leasing—applicability and purchase-comparison cap
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies to all leased ADPE except as components of an end item to be delivered to the Government. If the contractor leased ADPE but cannot demonstrate, on the basis of facts at time of decision and documented per paragraph (d), that leasing will result in less cost to the Government over the anticipated useful life, then rental costs are allowable only up to the amount that the contractor would be allowed had he purchased the ADPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leasing allowable only when leasing demonstrably cheaper to Government over useful life; otherwise cap rental allowability at equivalent purchase-allowed amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADPE leasing—annual demonstration criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Leasing costs are allowable only to the extent the contractor can annually demonstrate that: (i) they are reasonable and necessary given contractor requirements, comparable facility costs, lease types and rental agreement provisions; (ii) they do not give rise to a material equity in the facilities (no bargain options, etc.) but represent charges for current use including incidental service costs; and (iii) if total leasing cost reimbursed under cost-reimbursement contracts, or if total leasing cost in a single plant exceeds $500,000 per year and 50 percent or more is allocated to cost-reimbursement contracts, contracting officer approval was obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual documented demonstration required; watch for material equity, large-dollar thresholds ($500,000 and 50% allocation) that trigger contracting officer approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADPE sale-and-leaseback conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rental costs under a sale and leaseback arrangement shall be allowable only up to the amount the contractor would be allowed had he retained title to the ADPE, except where it is determined that leasing was the appropriate method of acquisition and the sale and leaseback (i) immediately followed acquisition and results in Government cost lower than other reasonably available leasing arrangements, or (ii) is otherwise in the best interests of the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sale-and-leaseback normally capped at retained-title equivalent; exceptions only when leasing clearly appropriate and advantageous to Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADPE useful-life estimation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An estimate of the anticipated useful life of ADPE may represent application life (utility in a given function), technological life (utility before becoming obsolete), or physical life (utility before wearing out), depending on facts. Application life usable if facility has utility only in a given function and duration determinable; technological life usable if contractor demonstrates replacement needed because of specific program objectives, identifiable cost reductions, increased workload volume, or consistent pattern of capacity (e.g., 2–3 shifts). Technological advances per se do not justify replacement before end of physical life if existing facilities can satisfy future requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose life-estimate basis (application/technological/physical) with supporting demonstration; technological obsolescence must be justified by concrete program/capacity/cost reasons, not mere advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADPE leasing—pre-acquisition justification documentation required
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor’s justification of leasing decisions shall consist of but is not limited to: (1) analysis of utilization of existing ADPE; (2) application of the criteria in paragraph (b); (3) specific objectives/requirements (data system study and specification); (4) solicitation of proposals from qualified sources based on the data system specification; (5) proposals received and reasons for selection of chosen equipment and for decision to lease. Annual justification of retention or change must include current data as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain contemporaneous documentation (analysis, solicitations, proposals, selection rationale, objective specs) prepared prior to acquisition and updated annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment cap for Article 139 claims
rubrics_metrics.description: No assessment in excess of $250 will be made against the pay of any one offender for a single act or incident, without approval of The Judge Advocate General or his designee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary assessment against service member pay under Article 139 limited to $250 per offender per incident unless higher-level approval obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 139 claims—time limit for claim submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint must be submitted within 60 days of the date of the incident out of which the claim arose, unless the commander acting on the report determines that good cause has been shown for the delay. The commander's determination that good cause has not been shown is final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 60-day filing window for claims under Article 139, with commander discretion for excusing delay; commander decision is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 139 claims—compensable and non-compensable categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims payable are limited to: (1) damage to/loss/destruction of property caused by riotous/violent/disorderly conduct or acts of depredation by Army members or acts implying willful damage; and (2) claims for property wrongfully taken (larceny, forgery, embezzlement, fraud, misappropriation) where wrongful taking involved. Claims not payable include claims payable under other regulations, claims from simple negligence, subrogee claims, personal injury/death, any portion covered by insurance, acts within scope of employment, and claims where claimant's negligence contributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict scope: willful acts and wrongful takings covered; negligence, insurance-covered portions, and other categories excluded.
